NASB.1: There is an appointed time for everything. And there is a time for every event under heaven--
NASB.2: A time to give birth and a time to die; A time to plant and a time to uproot what is planted.
NASB.3: A time to kill and a time to heal; A time to tear down and a time to build up.
NASB.4: A time to weep and a time to laugh; A time to mourn and a time to dance.
NASB.5: A time to throw stones and a time to gather stones; A time to embrace and a time to shun embracing.
NASB.6: A time to search and a time to give up as lost; A time to keep and a time to throw away.
NASB.7: A time to tear apart and a time to sew together; A time to be silent and a time to speak.
NASB.8: A time to love and a time to hate; A time for war and a time for peace.
NASB.9: What profit is there to the worker from that in which he toils?
NASB.10: I have seen the task which God has given the sons of men with which to occupy themselves.
NASB.11: He has made everything appropriate in its time. He has also set eternity in their heart, yet so that man will not find out the work which God has done from the beginning even to the end.
NASB.12: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and to do good in one's lifetime;
NASB.13: moreover, that every man who eats and drinks sees good in all his labor-- it is the gift of God.
NASB.14: I know that everything God does will remain forever; there is nothing to add to it and there is nothing to take from it, for God has [so] worked that men should fear Him.
NASB.15: That which is has been already and that which will be has already been, for God seeks what has passed by.
NASB.16: Furthermore, I have seen under the sun [that] in the place of justice there is wickedness and in the place of righteousness there is wickedness.
NASB.17: I said to myself, 'God will judge both the righteous man and the wicked man,' for a time for every matter and for every deed is there.
NASB.18: I said to myself concerning the sons of men, 'God has surely tested them in order for them to see that they are but beasts.'
NASB.19: For the fate of the sons of men and the fate of beasts is the same. As one dies so dies the other; indeed, they all have the same breath and there is no advantage for man over beast, for all is vanity.
NASB.20: All go to the same place. All came from the dust and all return to the dust.
NASB.21: Who knows that the breath of man ascends upward and the breath of the beast descends downward to the earth?
NASB.22: I have seen that nothing is better than that man should be happy in his activities, for that is his lot. For who will bring him to see what will occur after him?

NKJV.1: To everything there is a season, A time for every purpose under heaven:
NKJV.2: A time to be born, And a time to die; A time to plant, And a time to pluck what is planted;
NKJV.3: A time to kill, And a time to heal; A time to break down, And a time to build up;
NKJV.4: A time to weep, And a time to laugh; A time to mourn, And a time to dance;
NKJV.5: A time to cast away stones, And a time to gather stones;  A time to embrace, And a time to refrain from embracing;
NKJV.6: A time to gain, And a time to lose; A time to keep, And a time to throw away;
NKJV.7: A time to tear, And a time to sew;  A time to keep silence, And a time to speak;
NKJV.8: A time to love, And a time to hate; A time of war, And a time of peace.
NKJV.9: What profit has the worker from that in which he labors?
NKJV.10: I have seen the God-given task with which the sons of men are to be occupied.
NKJV.11: He has made everything beautiful in its time. Also He has put eternity in their hearts, except that no one can find out the work that God does from beginning to end.
NKJV.12: I know that nothing is better for them than to rejoice, and to do good in their lives,
NKJV.13: and also that every man should eat and drink and enjoy the good of all his labor—it is the gift of God.
NKJV.14: I know that whatever God does, It shall be forever. Nothing can be added to it, And nothing taken from it. God does it, that men should fear before Him.
NKJV.15: That which is has already been, And what is to be has already been; And God requires an account of what is past.
NKJV.16: Moreover I saw under the sun: In the place of judgment, Wickedness was there; And in the place of righteousness, Iniquity was there.
NKJV.17: I said in my heart, “God shall judge the righteous and the wicked, For there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.”
NKJV.18: I said in my heart, “Concerning the condition of the sons of men, God tests them, that they may see that they themselves are like animals.”
NKJV.19: For what happens to the sons of men also happens to animals; one thing befalls them: as one dies, so dies the other. Surely, they all have one breath; man has no advantage over animals, for all is vanity.
NKJV.20: All go to one place: all are from the dust, and all return to dust.
NKJV.21: Who knows the spirit of the sons of men, which goes upward, and the spirit of the animal, which goes down to the earth?
NKJV.22: So I perceived that nothing is better than that a man should rejoice in his own works, for that is his heritage. For who can bring him to see what will happen after him?

ESV.1: For everything there is a season, and a time for every matter under heaven:
ESV.2: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up what is planted;
ESV.3: a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
ESV.4: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
ESV.5: a time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
ESV.6: a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;
ESV.7: a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
ESV.8: a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.
ESV.9: What gain has the worker from his toil?
ESV.10: I have seen the business that God has given to the children of man to be busy with.
ESV.11: He has made everything beautiful in its time. Also, he has put eternity into man's heart, yet so that he cannot find out what God has done from the beginning to the end.
ESV.12: I perceived that there is nothing better for them than to be joyful and to do good as long as they live;
ESV.13: also that everyone should eat and drink and take pleasure in all his toil — this is God's gift to man.
ESV.14: I perceived that whatever God does endures forever; nothing can be added to it, nor anything taken from it. God has done it, so that people fear before him.
ESV.15: That which is, already has been; that which is to be, already has been; and God seeks what has been driven away.
ESV.16: Moreover, I saw under the sun that in the place of justice, even there was wickedness, and in the place of righteousness, even there was wickedness.
ESV.17: I said in my heart, God will judge the righteous and the wicked, for there is a time for every matter and for every work.
ESV.18: I said in my heart with regard to the children of man that God is testing them that they may see that they themselves are but beasts.
ESV.19: For what happens to the children of man and what happens to the beasts is the same; as one dies, so dies the other. They all have the same breath, and man has no advantage over the beasts, for all is vanity.
ESV.20: All go to one place. All are from the dust, and to dust all return.
ESV.21: Who knows whether the spirit of man goes upward and the spirit of the beast goes down into the earth?
ESV.22: So I saw that there is nothing better than that a man should rejoice in his work, for that is his lot. Who can bring him to see what will be after him?

WEB.1: For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:
WEB.2: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;
WEB.3: a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
WEB.4: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
WEB.5: a time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
WEB.6: a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;
WEB.7: a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
WEB.8: a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.
WEB.9: What profit has he who works in that in which he labors?
WEB.10: I have seen the burden which God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted with.
WEB.11: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can’t find out the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end.
WEB.12: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice, and to do good as long as they live.
WEB.13: Also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy good in all his labor, is the gift of God.
WEB.14: I know that whatever God does, it shall be forever. Nothing can be added to it, nor anything taken from it; and God has done it, that men should fear before him.
WEB.15: That which is has been long ago, and that which is to be has been long ago: and God seeks again that which is passed away.
WEB.16: Moreover I saw under the sun, in the place of justice, that wickedness was there; and in the place of righteousness, that wickedness was there.
WEB.17: I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked; for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.”
WEB.18: I said in my heart, “As for the sons of men, God tests them, so that they may see that they themselves are like animals.
WEB.19: For that which happens to the sons of men happens to animals. Even one thing happens to them. As the one dies, so the other dies. Yes, they have all one breath; and man has no advantage over the animals: for all is vanity.
WEB.20: All go to one place. All are from the dust, and all turn to dust again.
WEB.21: Who knows the spirit of man, whether it goes upward, and the spirit of the animal, whether it goes downward to the earth?”
WEB.22: Therefore I saw that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his works; for that is his portion: for who can bring him to see what will be after him?

and a time for every activity under heaven: ⓕ

a time to give birth and a time to die; ⓖ
a time to plant and a time to uproot; [1]

a time to kill and a time to heal;
a time to tear down and a time to build;

a time to weep and a time to laugh; ⓗ

a time to throw stones and a time to gather stones; ⓙ

a time to keep and a time to throw away;

a time to be silent and a time to speak; ⓛ

a time to love and a time to hate;
a time for war and a time for peace. ⓜ
CSB17.9: What does the worker gain from his struggles? <sup>ⓝ</sup>

CSB17.11: He has made everything appropriate <sup>[2]</sup> in its time. <sup>ⓑ</sup> He has also put eternity in their hearts, <sup>[3]</sup> but no one can discover the work God has done from beginning to end. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.12: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and enjoy the <sup>[4]</sup> good life.
CSB17.13: It is also the gift of God whenever anyone eats, drinks, and enjoys all his efforts. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.14: I know that everything God does will last forever; there is no adding to it or taking from it. <sup>ⓔ</sup> God works so that people will be in awe of him. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.15: Whatever is, has already been, <sup>ⓖ</sup> and whatever will be, already is. However, God seeks justice for the persecuted. <sup>[5]</sup>
CSB17.16: I also observed under the sun: there is wickedness at the place of judgment and there is wickedness at the place of righteousness. <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.17: I said to myself, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked, <sup>ⓘ</sup> since there is a time for every activity and every work.” <sup>ⓙ</sup>

CSB17.21: Who knows if the spirits of the children of Adam go upward and the spirits of animals go downward to the earth?

AMP.1: There is a season (a time appointed) for everything and a time for every delight and event or purpose under heaven—
AMP.2:
A time to be born and a time to die;
A time to plant and a time to uproot what is planted.
AMP.3:
A time to kill and a time to heal;
A time to tear down and a time to build up.
AMP.4:
A time to weep and a time to laugh;
A time to mourn and a time to dance.
AMP.5:
A time to throw away stones and a time to gather stones;
A time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing.
AMP.6:
A time to search and a time to give up as lost;
A time to keep and a time to throw away.
AMP.7:
A time to tear apart and a time to sew together;
A time to keep silent and a time to speak.
AMP.8:
A time to love and a time to hate;
A time for war and a time for peace.
AMP.9: What profit is there for the worker from that in which he labors?
AMP.10: I have seen the task which God has given to the sons of men with which to occupy themselves.
AMP.11: He has made everything beautiful and appropriate in its time. He has also planted eternity [a sense of divine purpose] in the human heart [a mysterious longing which nothing under the sun can satisfy, except God]—yet man cannot find out (comprehend, grasp) what God has done (His overall plan) from the beginning to the end.
AMP.12: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and to do good as long as they live;
AMP.13: and also that every man should eat and drink and see and enjoy the good of all his labor—it is the gift of God.
AMP.14: I know that whatever God does, it endures forever; nothing can be added to it nor can anything be taken from it, for God does it so that men will fear and worship Him [with awe-filled reverence, knowing that He is God].
AMP.15: That which is has already been, and that which will be has already been, for God seeks what has passed by [so that history repeats itself].
AMP.16: Moreover, I have seen under the sun that in the place of justice there is wickedness, and in the place of righteousness there is wickedness.
AMP.17: I said to myself, "God will judge both the righteous and the wicked," for there is a time [appointed] for every matter and for every deed.
AMP.18: I said to myself regarding the sons of men, "God is surely testing them in order for them to see that [by themselves, without God] they are [only] animals."
AMP.19: For the [earthly] fate of the sons of men and the fate of animals is the same. As one dies, so dies the other; indeed, they all have the same breath and there is no preeminence or advantage for man [in and of himself] over an animal, for all is vanity.
AMP.20: All go to the same place. All came from the dust and all return to the dust.
AMP.21: Who knows if the spirit of man ascends upward and the spirit of the animal descends downward to the earth?
AMP.22: So I have seen that there is nothing better than that a man should be happy in his own works and activities, for that is his portion (share). For who will bring him [back] to see what will happen after he is gone?

NLT.1:
For everything there is a season,
a time for every activity under heaven.
NLT.2:
A time to be born and a time to die.
A time to plant and a time to harvest.
NLT.3:
A time to kill and a time to heal.
A time to tear down and a time to build up.
NLT.4:
A time to cry and a time to laugh.
A time to grieve and a time to dance.
NLT.5:
A time to scatter stones and a time to gather stones.
A time to embrace and a time to turn away.
NLT.6:
A time to search and a time to quit searching.
A time to keep and a time to throw away.
NLT.7:
A time to tear and a time to mend.
A time to be quiet and a time to speak.
NLT.8:
A time to love and a time to hate.
A time for war and a time for peace.
NLT.9: What do people really get for all their hard work?
NLT.10: I have seen the burden God has placed on us all.
NLT.11: Yet God has made everything beautiful for its own time. He has planted eternity in the human heart, but even so, people cannot see the whole scope of God’s work from beginning to end.
NLT.12: So I concluded there is nothing better than to be happy and enjoy ourselves as long as we can.
NLT.13: And people should eat and drink and enjoy the fruits of their labor, for these are gifts from God.
NLT.14: And I know that whatever God does is final. Nothing can be added to it or taken from it. God’s purpose is that people should fear him.
NLT.15: What is happening now has happened before, and what will happen in the future has happened before, because God makes the same things happen over and over again.
NLT.16: I also noticed that under the sun there is evil in the courtroom. Yes, even the courts of law are corrupt!
NLT.17: I said to myself, “In due season God will judge everyone, both good and bad, for all their deeds.”
NLT.18: I also thought about the human condition — how God proves to people that they are like animals.
NLT.19: For people and animals share the same fate — both breathe and both must die. So people have no real advantage over the animals. How meaningless!
NLT.20: Both go to the same place — they came from dust and they return to dust.
NLT.21: For who can prove that the human spirit goes up and the spirit of animals goes down into the earth?
NLT.22: So I saw that there is nothing better for people than to be happy in their work. That is our lot in life. And no one can bring us back to see what happens after we die.

MSG.1: There's an opportune time to do things, a right time for everything on the earth:
MSG.2:
A right time for birth and another for death,
A right time to plant and another to reap,
MSG.3:
A right time to kill and another to heal,
A right time to destroy and another to construct,
MSG.4:
A right time to cry and another to laugh,
A right time to lament and another to cheer,
MSG.5:
A right time to make love and another to abstain,
A right time to embrace and another to part,
MSG.6:
A right time to search and another to count your losses,
A right time to hold on and another to let go,
MSG.7:
A right time to rip out and another to mend,
A right time to shut up and another to speak up,
MSG.8:
A right time to love and another to hate,
A right time to wage war and another to make peace.
MSG.9: But in the end, does it really make a difference what anyone does?
MSG.10: I've had a good look at what God has given us to do—busywork, mostly.
MSG.11: True, God made everything beautiful in itself and in its time—but he's left us in the dark, so we can never know what God is up to, whether he's coming or going.
MSG.12: I've decided that there's nothing better to do than go ahead and have a good time and get the most we can out of life.
MSG.13: That's it—eat, drink, and make the most of your job. It's God's gift.
MSG.14: I've also concluded that whatever God does, that's the way it's going to be, always. No addition, no subtraction. God's done it and that's it. That's so we'll quit asking questions and simply worship in holy fear.
MSG.15:
Whatever was, is.
Whatever will be, is.
That's how it always is with God.
MSG.16: I took another good look at what's going on: The very place of judgment—corrupt!
MSG.17: The place of righteousness—corrupt! I said to myself, "God will judge righteous and wicked." There's a right time for every thing, every deed—and there's no getting around it.
MSG.18: I said to myself regarding the human race, "God's testing the lot of us, showing us up as nothing but animals."
MSG.19: Humans and animals come to the same end—humans die, animals die. We all breathe the same air. So there's really no advantage in being human. None. Everything's smoke.
MSG.20: We all end up in the same place—we all came from dust, we all end up as dust.
MSG.21: Nobody knows for sure that the human spirit rises to heaven or that the animal spirit sinks into the earth.
MSG.22: So I made up my mind that there's nothing better for us men and women than to have a good time in whatever we do—that's our lot. Who knows if there's anything else to life?

NIV.1:
A Time for Everything
There is a time for everything,
and a season for every activity under heaven:
NIV.2:
a time to be born and a time to die,
a time to plant and a time to uproot,
NIV.3:
a time to kill and a time to heal,
a time to tear down and a time to build,
NIV.4:
a time to weep and a time to laugh,
a time to mourn and a time to dance,
NIV.5:
a time to scatter stones and a time to gather them,
a time to embrace and a time to refrain,
NIV.6:
a time to search and a time to give up,
a time to keep and a time to throw away,
NIV.7:
a time to tear and a time to mend,
a time to be silent and a time to speak,
NIV.8:
a time to love and a time to hate,
a time for war and a time for peace.
NIV.9: What does the worker gain from his toil?
NIV.10: I have seen the burden God has laid on men.
NIV.11: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the hearts of men; yet they cannot fathom what God has done from beginning to end.
NIV.12: I know that there is nothing better for men than to be happy and do good while they live.
NIV.13: That everyone may eat and drink, and find satisfaction in all his toil—this is the gift of God.
NIV.14: I know that everything God does will endure forever; nothing can be added to it and nothing taken from it. God does it so that men will revere him.
NIV.15:
Whatever is has already been,
and what will be has been before;
and God will call the past to account.
NIV.16:
And I saw something else under the sun:
In the place of judgment—wickedness was there,
in the place of justice—wickedness was there.
NIV.17:
I thought in my heart,
“God will bring to judgment
both the righteous and the wicked,
for there will be a time for every activity,
a time for every deed.”
NIV.18: I also thought, “As for men, God tests them so that they may see that they are like the animals.
NIV.19: Man’s fate is like that of the animals; the same fate awaits them both: As one dies, so dies the other. All have the same breath; man has no advantage over the animal. Everything is meaningless.
NIV.20: All go to the same place; all come from dust, and to dust all return.
NIV.21: Who knows if the spirit of man rises upward and if the spirit of the animal goes down into the earth?”
NIV.22: So I saw that there is nothing better for a man than to enjoy his work, because that is his lot. For who can bring him to see what will happen after him?

NET.1: For everything there is an appointed time, and an appropriate time for every activity on earth:
NET.2: A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to uproot what was planted;
NET.3: A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
NET.4: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance.
NET.5: A time to throw away stones, and a time to gather stones; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
NET.6: A time to search, and a time to give something up as lost; a time to keep, and a time to throw away;
NET.7: A time to rip, and a time to sew; a time to keep silent, and a time to speak.
NET.8: A time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.
NET.9: What benefit can a worker gain from his toil?
NET.10: I have observed the burden that God has given to people to keep them occupied.
NET.11: God has made everything fit beautifully in its appropriate time, but he has also placed ignorance in the human heart so that people cannot discover what God has ordained, from the beginning to the end of their lives.
NET.12: I have concluded that there is nothing better for people than to be happy and to enjoy themselves as long as they live,
NET.13: and also that everyone should eat and drink, and find enjoyment in all his toil, for these things are a gift from God.
NET.14: I also know that whatever God does will endure forever; nothing can be added to it, and nothing taken away from it. God has made it this way, so that men will fear him.
NET.15: Whatever exists now has already been, and whatever will be has already been; for God will seek to do again what has occurred in the past.
NET.16: I saw something else on earth: In the place of justice, there was wickedness, and in the place of fairness, there was wickedness.
NET.17: I thought to myself, “God will judge both the righteous and the wicked; for there is an appropriate time for every activity, and there is a time of judgment for every deed.
NET.18: I also thought to myself, “It is for the sake of people, so God can clearly show them that they are like animals.
NET.19: For the fate of humans and the fate of animals are the same: As one dies, so dies the other; both have the same breath. There is no advantage for humans over animals, for both are fleeting.
NET.20: Both go to the same place, both come from the dust, and to dust both return.
NET.21: Who really knows if the human spirit ascends upward, and the animal’s spirit descends into the earth?
NET.22: So I perceived there is nothing better than for people to enjoy their work, because that is their reward; for who can show them what the future holds?
